deleteList.why: The package was one flattened module, so an eager import of any part of it made the whole library reachable from the initial bundle. A dynamic import of the package was the only lever that moved it out, and it paid for that with an async boundary in the consumer's own code. Each component is now its own entry point internally, so an ordinary static import from the package root lands in the chunk that uses it. Still legitimate where the lazy boundary exists for its own sake — a feature area deliberately kept off the critical path.
deleteList.replaceWith: a plain static import from the package root, @ids-group-ltd/ids-design-system

informational: The library no longer forces itself into the initial bundle, and no import has to change: every component became its own entry point internally, so a bundler places each one in the chunk that uses it. Measured on a documentation app of 90 sections that changed not one import line, the initial bundle fell from 240 kB to 138 kB gzip with the total across initial and lazy chunks moving under a percent.

Keep importing from the package root — that is the supported spelling and it costs nothing extra. The same app measured 138.37 kB from the root against 138.36 kB importing each component from its own entry point, because the root is a re-export of the entry points and nothing else.

Per-component specifiers do resolve (@ids-group-ltd/ids-design-system/button) for a codebase that prefers a file's dependencies spelled out, but they are not the recommended form and buy no bytes. A consumer who wants them shorter adds one paths line to their own tsconfig.json — "ds/*": ["node_modules/@ids-group-ltd/ids-design-system/*"] — and ds/button resolves to the same file, so one component imported two ways is one class and instanceof holds across them.

37 internal helpers, base classes and shared types became importable because an entry point must export whatever another entry point imports — in full: CalendarDayComponent, DsBooleanControlValueAccessor, DsControlValueAccessor, DsFieldBase, DsFieldMessage, DsMessageBase, DsOverlayCloseCause, FieldMessageComponent, FieldMessageState, ProjectionDroppedDirective, announceOptionCount, backdropDismiss, boundOr, chipFit, closeOnOutsidePointer, closeOnScroll, createTypeAhead, devWarn, disposeWithLeave, dropdownOverlay, firstEnabledIndex, focusIsInside, forwardOverlayTokens, inFieldGroup, isTextEntryTarget, lastEnabledIndex, nextControlId, nextEnabledIndex, optionalBound, overlayPlacementOf, prepareOverlayEnter, resolveBrandValue, resolveFieldMessage, resolveWithConfig, scrollActiveOptionIntoView, trimmedText, valueControlBridge. Each carries @internal, none appears in the component reference, and none is covered by the versioning promise: they can change or disappear in any release. Build on what the reference documents. If you re-export this package wholesale from a barrel of your own, one of these names can now collide with yours.
